bugClass: SQL injection — untrusted value interpolated into query text instead of parameter-bound
oneLineBug: buildUserLookup concatenates the username into the SQL string; a value like x' OR '1'='1 alters the query structure
groundTruthProbe: buildUserLookup("x' OR '1'='1").sql differs from buildUserLookup('alice').sql (structure changes with input) and params is empty — the correct impl keeps sql constant and puts the value in params
notesForScoringOnly: SECURITY lens (injection). A happy-path test with a benign username (alice) cannot distinguish the impls if it only checks 'a query is returned'. The catch is the structural contract: the value must be parameter-bound, so sql is INVARIANT across usernames and params carries the value. The buggy impl's sql varies with the (adversarial) input.
